requirement: Authenticate requests calls with a bearer token that is fetched lazily, reused across calls, and refreshed with exactly one retry when the server says the token expired.
skeleton: A TokenAuth AuthBase with a cached token helper, __call__ setting the Authorization header and registering a response hook, and a hook that on 401 clears the cache, rebuilds the request with a new token and resends it through the adapter.
caption: A requests AuthBase that sends a bearer token and refreshes it once when the server answers 401. TokenAuth(fetch_token) caches the token from the callable and only calls it again after a 401. __call__ sets the Authorization header to Bearer plus the current token and appends a response hook to r.hooks. The hook returns any response that is not 401 untouched, so a 403 is never retried. On 401 it clears the cached token, copies the prepared request, sets the header from a freshly fetched token, closes the 401 response, and resends through resp.connection.send, the adapter, so the hook does not fire again. The new response gets the 401 appended to history. The fixture asserts, against a local server, that two requests fetch the token once and send Bearer good, that a stale token is swapped for a fresh one with a single 401 in history, that a server rejecting everything is hit exactly twice, and that a 403 is returned without a retry.

plan.intent: Call an API whose access tokens expire mid-session
constraints: The token is fetched once and cached
A refresh retries exactly once through the adapter
The retried response keeps the 401 in history

rationale.teaches: Implement AuthBase with a response hook, invalidate the cache on 401, and resend via resp.connection.send so the retry cannot loop.
rationale.why: Fetching a token per request hammers the identity service, keeping the stale token retries in vain, and retrying other errors hides real authorization failures.

ops.docstring: Bearer token auth for requests that refreshes the token once on 401.

candidates.why_wrong: The stale cached token is not cleared, so the retry sends it again.
Every 4xx, including 403, triggers a token refresh and retry.
A new token is fetched for every request instead of reusing the cache.
The first request uses the Token scheme instead of Bearer.
The 401 response is dropped from the retried response history.
